correctness.rationale: The frozen finite theorem is correct, but not accepted as new. In an independent exact reproduction (branches/variance_independent.py), the coefficient of x^k u^f in the product of 1+u[(1+x)^{a_i}−1] counted samples with f represented groups. Moment numerators and exhaustive decreasing partitions gave no failure up to 12 and one at 13, namely (1,6,6), with strict extrema at 3,5,6 as claimed. The repaired theorem retains only the infinite (1,m,m) family. The variance identity follows from the absence-indicator covariances; I verified both rational differences algebraically. The small-budget numerator has strictly positive coefficients after shifting m by 6. For the later rise, binomial growth B_{m+1}/B_m>3 and growth of the positive cubic L_{m+1}/L_m<2 preserve B_m>L_m from m=6, so the later difference is positive. Since m−1≥5, that rise follows the strict decline at 3→4. This is a proof for all m≥6 and does not claim exactly two strict peaks throughout the family. The independently written repaired checker at repairs/3/verify.py passed 95 exact sampling-distribution checks; the uploaded verifier was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: The original cutoff was already reported and is no longer claimed. The repair establishes that a decrease followed by renewed uncertainty is not a single small-community exception: every larger balanced pair of groups with a singleton in this natural family exhibits it. The proof identifies two separated sample budgets uniformly and explains why the later rise persists. This is useful for the conditional richness model without implying anything about empirical extinctions or a complete peak classification.
